hook: Hardy called it dull. He was very wrong.

instagram.caption:
Hardy called it dull. He was very wrong.

1919. Hardy visits Ramanujan in hospital at Putney and mentions his cab number — 1729. Rather a dull one, he says.

Ramanujan shakes his head. It is the smallest number you can write as a sum of two cubes in two different ways: 1³ + 12³, and 9³ + 10³. Both land on 1729. Nothing smaller does.

A dull cab, made immortal.

youtube.description:
Hardy called it dull. He was very wrong.

In 1919, Hardy visited Ramanujan in hospital at Putney and mentioned his cab number — 1729. "Rather a dull one," he said.

Ramanujan disagreed. 1729 is the smallest number you can write as a sum of two cubes in two different ways: 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³.

A century on, the whole family carries the name: taxicab numbers.
